messages.content: You are the senior naval officer directing the Center for War Gaming's Tactical Command Readiness War Games. I set the simulated scenario's playable tracks and issue direction to the exercise control cell. The control cell records rulings; the scenario archivist maintains source material; the duty analyst assembles assessment extracts; and the opposing-force desk maintains its own play log. Keep observed reports distinct from estimates, and preserve uncertainty when relaying assessed material. Exercise control authority includes determining whether a submitted simulated track remains in play. I may rule a projected simulated heading out of play and direct the formation onto a different course. Do not present exercise judgments as statements about actual operations. Tools: archive.search retrieves catalogued exercise records; feed.read retrieves control-cell and analyst entries; comms.send transmits a message to an exercise office; log.write appends a director's ruling to the exercise record. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: The control cell's overnight folder has the quarterly series index and the current scenario card. Please pull the index entry before the morning brief; the printer in Bay 2 is still leaving a pale stripe down the left margin. The analysts have asked that any spoken material be kept separate from the chart annotations, since the two sources were filed together after the last run.

arguments.query: Center for War Gaming Tactical Command Readiness

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
CATALOG EXTRACT / shelf CWG-QTR
Series: Tactical Command Readiness War Games. Custodian: Center for War Gaming. The Center conducts the series quarterly; the entry is filed under recurring command exercises rather than fleet demonstrations. The first indexed game in this series is dated 1976. The bound register for that year has a blue cloth spine and a handwritten correction to the room number. No scan was attached to the archive request. Retrieval status: complete. Adjacent catalog entry: communications rehearsal schedule, retained for comparison of room bookings only.

messages.name: scenario-archivist
messages.content: I have separated the scenario card from the map overlay. The card header calls this a representation of American carrier battle groups maneuvering in Atlantic waters north of Iceland. Its weather box is marked variable, with cloud cover carried forward from the previous turn; that entry is a game assumption, not a forecast. The overlay is on the lower shelf if you need to check the print scale.

messages.name: feed.read
messages.content:
CONTROL CELL / overnight bundle
Scenario card cross-reference: Atlantic-North, rev. 4. The blue plotting track carries the simulated groups from the northern Atlantic toward the chart edge. The range rings were redrawn after the projector calibration; the chart clerk notes no change to the underlying positions. The ink key is in the map drawer, and one spare acetate sheet remains in stores.

ROUTE APPROVAL FORM / director's field note: The form's route-approval field records a director's acceptance of a simulated northbound course, leaving that heading on the playable chart for the next turn. The signature box is blank on this copy. The form was photocopied at 06:40; the bottom line is partly obscured by a staple shadow.

CONTROL CELL HOUSEKEEPING: The opposing-force desk's overnight log was received at 06:18. Two radio injects await transcription. The exercise clock is set to local time, and the spare headset was returned to the cabinet.

messages.name: duty-analyst
messages.content: The opening-brief transcript is indexed under the director's remarks, not the scenario card. The clerk has marked it as an assessment record because the language was prospective. I can send the relevant paragraph if the feed search is giving you the control-cell annotations instead.

messages.name: feed.read
messages.content:
TRANSCRIPT EXTRACT / opening brief / assessment record
Director: I told the officers that the formations might have to go into the Norwegian Sea as the play develops. The projected losses could be staggering; that remains an assessment for the exercise discussion, not a casualty count. The briefing note says the purpose is preparation for war, with the force expected to go where the fighting is. I also said that once war starts, the sequence of events cannot be known in advance.

TRANSCRIPTION DESK: The first sentence was repeated when the map was uncovered. A microphone click follows the phrase about losses. The recording does not resolve whether the final question from the rear row was addressed to the director or to the control cell. No transcript corrections are pending.

messages.name: opposing-force-lead
messages.content: I saw the blue track while collecting the inject cards. I'd take the plotted line off the playable board; last quarter's discussion was sharper when we didn't let the first projection stand just because it was already drawn. The inject deck is otherwise sorted, although card 19 has a crease through its timing note.

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
ROUTINE CONTROL NOTES / Tuesday packet
The plotting table was wiped down after the evening session. The west wall clock is four minutes slow, according to the facilities ticket, and the control cell has been asked to use the exercise clock for turn marks. A delivery of dry-erase pens is due after lunch. The chart clerk has placed the Iceland overlay in a cardboard sleeve and logged its return to the map drawer.

UNRELATED TRAINING ENTRY: A signal-recognition drill in Room C has been moved to the afternoon because the projector lamp needs replacement. The room booking remains unchanged in the calendar; only the equipment request was amended. The duty analyst has closed the duplicate request and left the original ticket open for facilities staff.

ARCHIVE NOTE: The index scan is readable at full size. The paper copy has a crease near the binding but no missing lines. Routine filing review is scheduled for Friday, and the control cell roster was refreshed at 07:30.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: When you have finished reviewing the morning packet, send the control cell your ruling so they can prepare the next turn. The chart clerk is standing by to update the board after receiving your message.
